title: Fixed the context menu throwing under a Content Security Policy that enforces Trusted Types (`require-trusted-types-for 'script'`) when an item showed a check mark, which happened for "Read only", "Read-only comment", and any border already applied to the selection. The mark was built as an HTML string and written through `innerHTML`; it is now built as a DOM node, so the menu needs no Trusted Types policy and no `sanitizer`, and those items are announced to assistive technology as checkboxes, so their state is read out and not only drawn. A custom context menu or column menu item can show the same mark through a new `checked` option, which takes a boolean or a function returning one. Note that `checked` is now a reserved item property: an item that already carries one holding a boolean or a function is drawn with the mark and announced as a checkbox, so rename it to opt out, and drop any mark drawn inside `name` or the item shows two. See the migration guide.
